approvalProvenance.how: the repository owner pasted an explicit approval into the session: 'D-088 V1/V2 GLP1R HUMAN PREREGISTRATION IS APPROVED'
approvalProvenance.why_this_is_recorded: the preregistration's own rule requires a human seal. The approval arrived as a chat message, not a signature, so the exact form it took is written down here rather than asserted as a signature. A reader who disagrees that this constitutes a human seal can see precisely what was relied on.

prereg.motivationDetail: Found by code inspection, NOT by the V1 result. glp1rQsarV2.mjs carries the descriptor + peptide features, the A/B/C representation family and the calibration-only selection rule, but is reached ONLY by giprQsar.mjs. The GLP-1R axis runs glp1rQsar.trainAndValidate, which fits the ridge on Morgan bits alone. The GLP-1R axis has never reached its own V2 engine. This gap exists independently of how V1 scored.

priorEvidence.note: recorded as prior evidence for the reader. It is NOT an input to arm selection, and the selection code cannot see it.

arms.A: V1 — Morgan-only ridge, exactly as glp1rQsar.trainAndValidate runs today. Unchanged; re-run only to report it alongside B.
arms.B: V2 — the SAME engine giprQsar already uses, bound to the GLP-1R pin and the GLP-1R frozen gate. Descriptors + peptide features + Morgan bits, representation family A/B/C, selection on calibration MAE only.

prereg.armsAreExhaustive: No arm C. If neither clears the gate the result is BLOCKED, and a further arm requires a NEW human-sealed preregistration.

selectionRule.mechanism: selectRepresentation() structurally refuses any candidate object carrying a test metric — selecting on test is impossible, not merely forbidden
selectionRule.testMetricsReadOnce: exactly once, AFTER selection is permanently closed; reported, never fed back
selectionRule.harkGuard: any read of a test metric during the selection phase raises HARK_MISMATCH and ABORTS the experiment

splitIsolation.requirement: train, calib and test must be pairwise disjoint by canonicalSmiles AND by scaffold bucket
splitIsolation.enforcement: asserted at runtime before any fit; a violation ABORTS rather than warns
splitIsolation.standardization: fitted on TRAIN rows only; calib and test are transformed with train statistics and never contribute to them

frozenGateUntouched.statement: NOT ONE OF THESE MOVES. This experiment changes which ENGINE the axis runs, never what it must BEAT.

prereg.voidingRule: if the premise is falsified before any model is fitted (e.g. the V2 path turns out not to consume what it is believed to), the attempt is VOID with 0 consumed — the D-087 precedent

predictionsBeforeRunning.direction: UNKNOWN. More features is not automatically better: V2 adds descriptor columns to a 178-row training set, and a richer representation on a small peptide-heavy dataset can easily overfit and score WORSE on a scaffold-held-out test.
predictionsBeforeRunning.explicitlyNotPredicted: that arm B clears the gate
predictionsBeforeRunning.bothFailIsValid: BOTH ARMS FAILING IS A VALID AND SUCCESSFUL SCIENTIFIC OUTCOME. It would establish that this dataset and this model class do not meet the frozen bar, which is information, not defeat.

decisionRule.outcome: whatever applyFrozenGate returns for the selected arm stands
decisionRule.onFailure: the GLP-1R axis remains BLOCKED, NO_WINNER stands, and the honest conclusion is that the axis needs more human peptide rows rather than more engines
decisionRule.forbidden: re-running with a third representation, a different lambda, a different split seed, or any other knob, in search of a pass
